{"open_points":[
{"unit":"00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions","subject":"create a project / R0-38","kind":"contradiction","text":"create a project | owner; a service with a service token (today Cabinet Kernel) ... missing name refused","question":"Address is no longer required at creation, and only the owner may record an object. Yet R0-38 says a project has exactly one object. Does a project created by a service, or without an object, have no object, an empty object, or is creation refused until an object is given?","options":["object optional until the owner records it","create requires object data; services may supply it","an empty object is created with the project"],"default_guess":"Object is optional at creation and the owner records it later; 'exactly one' reads as 'at most one'."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions","subject":"correct a project vs record or correct a project's object","kind":"overlap","text":"the project with the new name, customer or object, next revision","question":"Is the object corrected through 'correct a project' or only through its own action? Whose revision moves (project, object or both), and which revision must the change state?","options":["object only via its own action, with its own revision","both paths; the project revision also moves"],"default_guess":"The object changes only via its own action and its own revision; the project correction covers name and customer."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions","subject":"R0-32 working-context confinement vs service-created projects","kind":"contradiction","text":"Operations with agent authority on a project are confined to the project of the current context","question":"Cabinet Kernel may create a project and add rooms, but its token carries agent authority confined to the working context. Can the agent create a new project? Can it list projects, validate ids or read projects outside the context? Does Kernel's own producer role (publishing) carry the same confinement, or does it have a separate token?","options":["agent creates nothing outside context; project creation by owner only","create allowed, other reads confined","Kernel holds two tokens: service and agent authority"],"default_guess":"With agent authority, Kernel cannot create projects and is confined to the context for all reads and writes. Listing and validation return only the context project."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions","subject":"read a project / list projects / read a project context","kind":"vague output","text":"a service, in its disclosure class (R0-26)","question":"The card and context contain `personal_data` (the object's address). What does a caller whose token does not allow `personal_data` (Kernel for the agent) get: the field omitted, a separate projection, or a refusal? How does this square with R0-04, which keeps the context answer field for field?","options":["fields above the class omitted","whole answer refused","separate projection operation per class"],"default_guess":"Offer a separate projection without `personal_data` fields. The full context stays field for field for tokens allowing `personal_data`."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Actors and trust boundaries: Actors and trust boundaries","subject":"who reads personal_data","kind":"contradiction","text":"Only the owner reads `personal_data` values.","question":"R0-26 lets a `personal_data` value leave Registry to a service whose token allows that class, and PresuPro and Portal read `context` with the address. Which is it? Which services may receive `personal_data`, and may any service read customer contact data, given that the customer actions list the owner only?","options":["owner plus services whose token allows the class","owner only; context drops address for services"],"default_guess":"The owner and the services whose token allows `personal_data` (PresuPro, Portal) receive it, for the address only. Customer contact data goes to the owner only."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions","subject":"switch request lifecycle","kind":"missing action","text":"a pending request the owner sees in the owner interface; the working context does not change","question":"What action confirms or declines a switch request? What does each produce, can several requests be pending, and do they expire?","options":["confirm/decline actions in the owner interface; one pending at a time","confirmation equals 'choose the working project'"],"default_guess":"Add owner actions 'confirm switch' (it makes a new context) and 'decline switch'. A new request replaces the pending one."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions","subject":"working context end","kind":"missing action","text":"none chosen, expired or withdrawn answers that there is none","question":"Which action withdraws a working context, and who takes it? What happens to the context when its project is archived, given that the context carries 'whether it is active'?","options":["owner action 'clear working context'; archiving keeps it with active=false","archiving withdraws the context"],"default_guess":"Add an owner action to withdraw the context. Archiving leaves the context in place with active=false, and agent writes are refused."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions","subject":"restrict processing","kind":"missing action","text":"restrict processing of a customer | owner | the Customer marked restricted","question":"Can a restriction be lifted, and by what action? Can a restricted customer still be corrected, erased, or named by a new project?","options":["owner action 'lift restriction'; correction and erasure allowed","restriction is final until erasure"],"default_guess":"Add an owner action to lift the restriction. Erasure and correction stay allowed, and new projects may name the customer."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions","subject":"R0-40 vs R0-03/R0-06","kind":"contradiction","text":"archived projects: five years after the project is closed ... erased or anonymised","question":"R0-06 calls customer erasure the only exception to 'Archiving never deletes; archived stays readable' (R0-03). R0-40 adds erasure or anonymisation of archived projects and objects. Which decision states the new exception? What do `validate`, read and the artifacts answer for an expired project?","options":["R0-40 narrows R0-03; validate answers archived with anonymised fields","R0-40 removes the project; validate answers not_found"],"default_guess":"R0-40 narrows R0-03 and R0-06: the id persists anonymised and `validate` still answers archived."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Primary actions: Primary actions","subject":"import a project with its identity","kind":"unnamed input","text":"the project under the identity it carries in its source ... after the owner checked the mapping","question":"What is the import's source: an export file, a running instance, or legacy stores? Through which surface does the owner run it? R0-34 forbids test-space ids in production, so may an id from a test instance's identity space enter production, or is it remapped?","options":["owner uploads an export in the owner interface; ids are kept only from legacy instances, remapped from test instances","an operator-run migration outside the API"],"default_guess":"The owner uploads an export file in the owner interface. Legacy ids are kept; test-instance ids are remapped to production ids under a mapping the owner confirms."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions","subject":"R0-29 owner interface scope","kind":"missing surface","text":"the project list, creating a project, reading and correcting its card ... and the customer, audit and switch-request views","question":"The owner acts only through the owner interface, yet R0-29 lists no view for publishing or withdrawing a pointer, recording an object, adding a room, import, restriction or erasure. Does the interface carry every owner action in the table, or does the owner reach some actions another way?","options":["the interface carries every owner action","some owner actions are dropped"],"default_guess":"The owner interface carries every action whose 'who' includes the owner."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Actors and trust boundaries: Actors and trust boundaries","subject":"location of Kernel, PresuPro, Cabinet","kind":"unnamed boundary","text":"the service API for services, reachable only on the production host and over the protected channel","question":"Where do Cabinet Kernel, PresuPro and Cabinet run, and over which channel do they reach Registry? If Kernel runs where an agent has access, how is the rule 'the agent holds no Registry service token' kept for Kernel's token?","options":["all on the production host","on the VPS through the same WireGuard tunnel","Kernel on the agent machine (breaks R0-25)"],"default_guess":"Kernel, PresuPro and Cabinet run on the production host or the VPS, never on a machine an agent administers. VPS services use the WireGuard tunnel."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Actors and trust boundaries: Actors and trust boundaries","subject":"test instances' authentication","kind":"scope gap","text":"Every request on either is authenticated ... Secrets — ... in the production instance's configuration","question":"Do authentication, disclosure classes and the 'agent never holds the owner credential' rule apply to test instances? An agent working on a test instance on its own machine would need some credential. Who holds it?","options":["same rules, with test-only credentials the agent may hold","test instances run without authentication"],"default_guess":"Test instances enforce the same rules with their own test-only credentials, which an agent may hold. These never equal production's."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Decisions: Decisions","subject":"R0-37 audit scope","kind":"vague","text":"Every significant operation leaves an audit entry","question":"Which operations are significant? All writes, reads of `personal_data`, sign-ins, refused requests, context choices and switch requests?","options":["all writes, all personal_data reads, sign-ins, context and switch events, refusals","writes only"],"default_guess":"Log all writes, reads of `personal_data`, sign-in attempts, context and switch events, and authorization refusals."},
{"unit":"00_product.md:Explicit exclusions: Explicit exclusions","subject":"onboard_object","kind":"contradiction","text":"a client of the API like any consumer ... its staff-credential use ends with R0-30","question":"R0-27 requires every caller to hold a token and lists no token for `onboard_object`. Does it get its own service token, or is it retired, its role taken by the interface and Kernel?","options":["retired","own service token with limited operations"],"default_guess":"`onboard_object` is retired. set_aside.subject: create a project / R0-38
set_aside.text: create a project | owner; a service with a service token (today Cabinet Kernel) ... missing name refused
set_aside.question: Address is no longer required at creation, and only the owner may record an object. Yet R0-38 says a project has exactly one object. Does a project created by a service, or without an object, have no object, an empty object, or is creation refused until an object is given?
options: object optional until the owner records it
create requires object data; services may supply it
an empty object is created with the project
set_aside.default_guess: Object is optional at creation and the owner records it later; 'exactly one' reads as 'at most one'.

set_aside.text: the project with the new name, customer or object, next revision

options: object only via its own action, with its own revision
both paths; the project revision also moves
set_aside.default_guess: The object changes only via its own action and its own revision; the project correction covers name and customer.

set_aside.subject: R0-32 working-context confinement vs service-created projects
set_aside.text: Operations with agent authority on a project are confined to the project of the current context
set_aside.question: Cabinet Kernel may create a project and add rooms, but its token carries agent authority confined to the working context. Can the agent create a new project? Can it list projects, validate ids or read projects outside the context? Does Kernel's own producer role (publishing) carry the same confinement, or does it have a separate token?
options: agent creates nothing outside context; project creation by owner only
create allowed, other reads confined
Kernel holds two tokens: service and agent authority
set_aside.default_guess: With agent authority, Kernel cannot create projects and is confined to the context for all reads and writes. Listing and validation return only the context project.

What does a caller whose token does not allow `personal_data` (Kernel for the agent) get: the field omitted, a separate projection, or a refusal? How does this square with R0-04, which keeps the context answer field for field?
options: fields above the class omitted
whole answer refused
separate projection operation per class
set_aside.default_guess: Offer a separate projection without `personal_data` fields. The full context stays field for field for tokens allowing `personal_data`.

set_aside.subject: who reads personal_data

Which services may receive `personal_data`, and may any service read customer contact data, given that the customer actions list the owner only?
options: owner plus services whose token allows the class
owner only; context drops address for services
set_aside.default_guess: The owner and the services whose token allows `personal_data` (PresuPro, Portal) receive it, for the address only. Customer contact data goes to the owner only.

confirmation equals 'choose the working project'
set_aside.default_guess: Add owner actions 'confirm switch' (it makes a new context) and 'decline switch'. A new request replaces the pending one.

options: owner action 'clear working context'; archiving keeps it with active=false
archiving withdraws the context
set_aside.default_guess: Add an owner action to withdraw the context. Archiving leaves the context in place with active=false, and agent writes are refused.

options: owner action 'lift restriction'; correction and erasure allowed
restriction is final until erasure
set_aside.default_guess: Add an owner action to lift the restriction. Erasure and correction stay allowed, and new projects may name the customer.

set_aside.subject: R0-40 vs R0-03/R0-06
set_aside.text: archived projects: five years after the project is closed ... erased or anonymised
set_aside.question: R0-06 calls customer erasure the only exception to 'Archiving never deletes; archived stays readable' (R0-03). R0-40 adds erasure or anonymisation of archived projects and objects. Which decision states the new exception? What do `validate`, read and the artifacts answer for an expired project?
options: R0-40 narrows R0-03; validate answers archived with anonymised fields
R0-40 removes the project; validate answers not_found

set_aside.subject: import a project with its identity
set_aside.text: the project under the identity it carries in its source ... after the owner checked the mapping
set_aside.question: What is the import's source: an export file, a running instance, or legacy stores? Through which surface does the owner run it? R0-34 forbids test-space ids in production, so may an id from a test instance's identity space enter production, or is it remapped?
options: owner uploads an export in the owner interface; ids are kept only from legacy instances, remapped from test instances
an operator-run migration outside the API
set_aside.default_guess: The owner uploads an export file in the owner interface. Legacy ids are kept; test-instance ids are remapped to production ids under a mapping the owner confirms.

set_aside.subject: R0-29 owner interface scope
set_aside.text: the project list, creating a project, reading and correcting its card ... and the customer, audit and switch-request views
set_aside.question: The owner acts only through the owner interface, yet R0-29 lists no view for publishing or withdrawing a pointer, recording an object, adding a room, import, restriction or erasure. Does the interface carry every owner action in the table, or does the owner reach some actions another way?
options: the interface carries every owner action
some owner actions are dropped
set_aside.default_guess: The owner interface carries every action whose 'who' includes the owner.

set_aside.unit: 00_product.md:Actors and trust boundaries: Actors and trust boundaries
set_aside.subject: location of Kernel, PresuPro, Cabinet
set_aside.text: the service API for services, reachable only on the production host and over the protected channel
set_aside.question: Where do Cabinet Kernel, PresuPro and Cabinet run, and over which channel do they reach Registry? If Kernel runs where an agent has access, how is the rule 'the agent holds no Registry service token' kept for Kernel's token?
options: all on the production host
on the VPS through the same WireGuard tunnel
Kernel on the agent machine (breaks R0-25)
set_aside.default_guess: Kernel, PresuPro and Cabinet run on the production host or the VPS, never on a machine an agent administers. VPS services use the WireGuard tunnel.

set_aside.unit: 00_product.md:Actors and trust boundaries: Actors and trust boundaries
set_aside.subject: test instances' authentication
set_aside.text: Every request on either is authenticated ... Secrets — ... in the production instance's configuration
set_aside.question: Do authentication, disclosure classes and the 'agent never holds the owner credential' rule apply to test instances? An agent working on a test instance on its own machine would need some credential. Who holds it?
options: same rules, with test-only credentials the agent may hold
test instances run without authentication
set_aside.default_guess: Test instances enforce the same rules with their own test-only credentials, which an agent may hold. These never equal production's.

set_aside.subject: R0-37 audit scope
set_aside.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
set_aside.question: Which operations are significant? All writes, reads of `personal_data`, sign-ins, refused requests, context choices and switch requests?
options: all writes, all personal_data reads, sign-ins, context and switch events, refusals
writes only
set_aside.default_guess: Log all writes, reads of `personal_data`, sign-in attempts, context and switch events, and authorization refusals.

set_aside.subject: onboard_object
set_aside.text: a client of the API like any consumer ... its staff-credential use ends with R0-30
set_aside.question: R0-27 requires every caller to hold a token and lists no token for `onboard_object`. Does it get its own service token, or is it retired, its role taken by the interface and Kernel?
options: retired
own service token with limited operations
set_aside.default_guess: `onboard_object` is retired. It gets no token, and any call it makes is refused.
